chapter_mission: Ben visits the Foundation. Aelia is warm, prepared, legitimate, and hard to attack because the charity’s public work is real. Add a genuine charity warmth beat: she remembers a scholarship recipient, corrects a child’s name, notices a veteran’s discomfort, or writes a condolence note by hand while Ben watches. She gently makes Ben feel young and underprepared. Civilian-awkwardness beat: While waiting to see Aelia, Ben is offered tea or water by a young Foundation staffer who clearly recognizes him but is trying to be professional. Ben over-explains why he is there, then catches himself and goes quiet. The staffer notices and is polite about it. This is the second of two recognition-bracing moments (the first was the Civitas lunchroom), and it pays off Aelia’s later social victory — Ben is already on the back foot before he sits down with her.
